title: Microbatch playbook scratch — Victor C.
content:
Shift snapshot (evening, ~18:30) — quick brain dump before sleep.

Goal: keep a concise, runnable playbook for investigating small-batch p99 spikes and to capture experiments that are cheap to run in CI/qa. This is not the final playbook — iterative notes.

1) Observed symptoms
- ~18:05 UTC: queued microbatch workload (seq_len mean 128, 95th 512) — saw p99 token latency increase from ~90ms -> 210ms on a small subset of requests.
- Affected route: /v1/generate (model: rwd-4b-optim).
- Breakdown from console: kernel time up, CPU spike on driver process, GPU utilization steady ~56%.
- Error rate: 0.0, no OOMs. KV cache hit rate temporarily dipped ~12% -> 3% for those requests.

2) Quick hypothesis (order of likelihood)
- KV-cache eviction thrash when microbatches interleave with long context requests -> extra recompute.
- Suboptimal batching window alignment (small batches + long tail = bad packing).
- A kernel stall on cuBLAS path when sequence length hopping happens; could be a kernel-selection jitter.
- Priority preemption from background maintenance job (compaction/GC) on the node.

3) Quick repro steps (local/qa)
- Repro case script: tools/repro/microbatch_tail_probe.sh (WIP). Steps:
  a) Spawn 50 concurrent clients with Poisson arrival (lambda tuned) hitting seq_len distribution: mix short(32) and long(512) at 15:1 ratio.
  b) Pin to same model variant and host via routing header X-RW-PIN.
  c) Collect per-token latencies from client-side and server token timestamps (enable RT_TRACE=1).
- Local run note: use --no-cache to simulate cold start vs warm runs.

4) Instrumentation to run now (in order)
- Enable kv_cache.metrics=debug for 5m on a single node in staging; watch eviction_count and eviction_depth.
- Attach perf (or Linux ftrace) to runtime worker thread for ~30s during repro. Collect perf record -> flame graph.
- Increase batching window from 8ms -> 20ms on one QA pool and compare effective batch sizes + p50/p95/p99.
- Toggle prefix caching: set prefix_kv_mode=local-only vs shared-cache to compare.

5) Commands / snippets I used today (save):
- run repro (quick): 
  ./tools/repro/microbatch_tail_probe.sh --clients 50 --duration 300 --mix "short:32:45,long:512:5" --pin-host host-09
- enable kv debug on node host-09: 
  curl -X POST "http://host-09:8080/admin/config" -d '{"kv_cache.metrics":"debug"}'
- collect flame graph (on node):
  sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30
  sudo perf script > out.perf
  ./scripts/stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf | ./scripts/flamegraph.pl > perf.svg

6) Small experiments to try (ranked, quick to roll back)
- EXP A: Increase batching window to 20ms for a minute; check throughput drop vs p99 improvement. (Risk: small throughput regression)
- EXP B: Force-use local KV cache and pin long-context requests to separate pool (costly routing change).
- EXP C: Try alternative kernel-selection table (fallback heuristic) on one node (requires build flag).
- EXP D: Temporarily lower worker thread scheduling priority for maintenance jobs (nice +10) to see if preemption is to blame.

7) Quick triage checklist (items I did / to do)
- [x] Reproduced p99 bump in staging with script above (18:20).
- [x] Collected perf trace + kv metrics (attach out.perf and kv_dump).
- [ ] Run EXP A in QA pool (need a small maintenance window).
- [ ] Open a small canary with kernel-selection toggle (PR draft created: linked).
- [ ] Sync with Lina on rollout plan for caching knob.
- [ ] Add a guardrail in routing to avoid mixing very long sequences into microbatch pools.

8) Notes for the kernel-level oddities
- Flame graph shows 40% of time in function runtime::kloop::prepare_kernels -> hint at kernel selection.
- Stack traces sometimes show cudaStreamSynchronize in unusual contexts (maybe stray host waits while waiting for KV loads).
- One sample trace had repeated memcpy H2D around token 200 of a request — could be evicted cache page being pulled mid-request.

9) Notes to self / follow-ups for tomorrow
- Build a minimal instrumentation that logs per-request KV access pattern (list of cache keys accessed) — keep lightweight (probabilistic sampling).
- Add a one-line note to the playbook: "If kv_cache_hit_rate drops <5% for >30s, shift traffic to long-context-capable pool."
- Draft a short runbook entry for SRE to flip batching window and revert.
- Pair with Maya tomorrow 09:30 to go over kernel flame graph and hypothesis C.

10) Meeting / communication bullets (for triage thread)
- TL;DR: transient p99 increase traced to low KV hit-rate + kernel selection jitter on mixed microbatch/long-context workload. Repro steps + immediate mitigations attached.
- Ask SRE: can we reserve a small QA pool with batching_window=20ms for 1h?
- Ask Product: any expected traffic patterns that would cause bursty long-context requests on this route?

11) Anything weird I noticed unrelated to main issue
- One node (host-12) has a nightly cron that runs repo maintenance at 03:00 but logs show a failed attempt at 17:58 (we need to validate cron behavior).
- Noticed small memory leak in worker process after ~6h in staging (heap grows ~70MB). TODO file a follow-up.

Raw scratch ideas (freeform):
- Maybe a small hybrid: route long-context warm clients to a dedicated pool with disabled microbatching, and let microbatch pool only take requests under 256 tokens. Could be a temporary safeguard.
- Consider a batching-window auto-tuner: watch seq_len hist + kv_hit_rate and adjust window to maximize tokens-per-batch subject to p90 latency SLO. Low priority but nice to have.

Attachments (where I stored outputs locally):
- /tmp/victor/microbatch/perf.out.perf (perf capture)
- /tmp/victor/microbatch/kv_dump_20260312.json
- Gist with traces: https://gist.github.com/victorchen/abc123-microbatch

End of shift. Quick wins tomorrow: run EXP A, pair with Maya, open INF ticket for kernel-selection review.

-- Victor C.
